Senses.Explanation: Old man Śākyamuni: a familiar name-form that repeatedly removes ceremonial distance in the Chan record. Longji Shaoxiu raises his staff and cries, “Old man Śākyamuni has arrived!” (釋迦老子來也) as his answer to “What is great function appearing?” (如何是大用現前). Dahui Zonggao likewise raises the whisk and says that the old man has arrived, then asks whether the assembly sees him. Shoushan Xingnian says that even if old man Śākyamuni came there, he would receive thirty blows; Dahui comments on a story of Śākyamuni disputing the buddha-teaching with Indra by saying, “This old fellow deserves thirty staff-blows” (這老漢好與三十拄杖). The form also remains a quotation label: Yunmen Wenyan says, “Old man Śākyamuni has already spoken; Maitreya still does not know” (釋迦老子道了也，彌勒猶自不知). Shanhui says, “Speak a sentence where old man Śākyamuni could not speak; take a step where the great teacher Bodhidharma could not go” (釋迦老子說不到處，說取一句；達磨大師行不到處，行取一步). Yuanwu Keqin quotes old man Śākyamuni’s saying about one person truly returning to the source, contrasts Wuzu Fayan’s version, and then supplies his own wording. The strongest coarse appraisal is textual and explicit: Deshan Xuanjian says, “Śākyamuni is a dry shit-stick” (釋迦老子是乾屎橛), paired with “Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra are shit-carrying fellows” (文殊普賢是擔屎漢). The deviation lies in the form’s repeated Chan use: a revered name becomes an immediately addressable “old man” whom named masters quote, enact, out-say, rebuke, and strike in public discourse.
Senses.Note: The exact longer form occurs 2,409 times in 281 allowlisted files. The suffix “old man” (老子) is translated rather than omitted: it is what distinguishes this headword from bare “Śākyamuni” (釋迦). The examples preserve separate deployment classes—quotation label, enacted arrival, comparison, rebuke, and coarse appraisal—rather than treating every overlap with the shorter name as equivalent.

Occurrences.Kwic: 達磨是老臊胡。釋迦老子是乾屎橛。文殊普賢是擔屎漢。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元), Deshan Xuanjian section: in his own hall address Deshan calls old man Shakyamuni a dry shit-stick.

Occurrences.Kwic: 大用現前。不存軌則。時有僧問。如何是大用現前。師拈起拄杖。高聲唱曰。釋迦老子來也。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Five Lamps Meeting at the Source (五燈會元), Longji Shaoxiu section. Asked “What is great function appearing?”, Longji Shaoxiu raises his staff and loudly cries, “Old man Śākyamuni has arrived!”

Occurrences.Kwic: 復舉起云。釋迦老子來也。還見麼。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Dahui Pujue (大慧普覺禪師語錄). After striking the Chan seat with the whisk and raising it again, Dahui Zonggao says, “Old man Śākyamuni has arrived! Do you see him?”

Occurrences.Kwic: 直饒釋迦老子到這裏也與三十棒
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Old Recorded Sayings of Venerable Masters (古尊宿語錄): Shoushan Xingnian says in his own named record that even old Shakyamuni arriving here would receive thirty blows.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師云釋迦老子道了也彌勒猶自不知
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of the Old Worthies (古尊宿語錄), Yunmen Wenyan section. After an elder asks how to discern at all times, Yunmen Wenyan says, “Old man Śākyamuni has already spoken; Maitreya still does not know.”

Occurrences.Kwic: 釋迦老子說不到處，說取一句；達磨大師行不到處，行取一步。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Shanhui (山暉禪師語錄), in Shanhui's small convocation. Shanhui is the exact speaker who raises his whisk and tells the assembly to speak a sentence where Shakyamuni Buddha could not speak and take a step where Bodhidharma could not go. Shakyamuni Buddha and Bodhidharma are the two masters named as limits surpassed in Shanhui's challenge, not the speaker of the stored sentence.

Occurrences.Kwic: 釋迦老子與天帝釋。在中庭裏相爭佛法甚鬧。師云。這老漢好與三十拄杖。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Dahui Pujue (大慧普覺禪師語錄) explicitly introduces the older saying with ‘Yunmen said’ (雲門道): Yunmen Wenyan says that old man Shakyamuni and Indra encounter one another; Dahui comments afterward.

Occurrences.Kwic: 復云：釋迦老子道：若有一人發真歸源，十方虗空悉皆消殞。五祖和尚又云：一人發真歸源，十方虗空磕著築著。山僧即不然，若有一人發真歸源，十方虗空錦上鋪花。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Record of the Ancestral Guidelines (列祖提綱錄), Yuanwu Keqin’s first-day-of-the-eighth-month hall address. Yuanwu quotes old man Śākyamuni saying that if one person truly returns to the source, the ten directions of empty space all vanish; he contrasts Wuzu Fayan and then supplies his own wording.
